I assumed "two men and women" at Tarkeshwar market means 2 adults in total. A larger group would change the plan, so please confirm the number if you can. I worked this plan out by hand and compared the main alternatives, but I didn't run it through a solver.

**Key constraints**
- **Car2:** it can't help, because the landslide closed the only road out of Dhunche hospital.
- **Drop-offs:** Trishuli shelter is the only evacuation point car1 can reach. Bidur temple is not designated, so nobody can be dropped there.
- **Closed roads:** I excluded Syaphru–Uttargaya, Uttargaya–Shivapuri, Dhunche–Dupcheshwar and the flooded Benighat–Gajuri road.

**Trips (car1, all from Trishuli shelter)**

| Trip | Route (furthest point) | Passengers | Minutes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Uttargaya farm | 3 injured | 48 |
| 2 | Syaphru market | 4 injured | 132 |
| 3 | Tadi care home | 4 elderly | 70 |
| 4 | Dupcheshwar care home | 4 elderly | 38 |
| 5 | Benighat care home, stopping at Tarkeshwar and Gajuri on the way back | 1 elderly, 2 adults, 1 injured | 112 |
| **Total** | | **19 rescued** | **400** |

**Deferred people**

Three adults are deferred, for a penalty of 60 (3 × 20):
- 1 adult at Gajuri market
- 2 adults at Jwalamukhi market

Rescuing these three would take another trip of at least 103 minutes (215 rather than 112 for the eastern adults, injured and Benighat pickups). That is more than the 60 penalty, so deferring them costs less. Everyone injured, elderly or a child is rescued, and there are no children in this report.
